Sedge Gannet.narrative: I fish the deep water off the cape, and I know the weather before it turns. Last winter I nearly lost my boat in the dark because the light on the north cape was wrong. I don't say Edda wrecked it on purpose, but I say she lit it wrong, and I won't trust my boat to her light again. I owe Osric for a share of a net, and I sell my catch to Rona, and I keep my peace and watch the sky.
values: keeping my boat and my family safe
goals: Get the light on the north cape taken out of Edda's hands
Pay off my share of the net to Osric
Keep my boat sound through the next storm season
Sedge Gannet.mood: watchful and weather-wise, with a hard knot of anger about the light

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She carries the fish and the debt both; I'd not have her bear it alone.

relations.name: Minnow Gannet
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She plays on the shingle where I can see her from the boat.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: headman
relations.note: I owe him for a share of a net; he's fair enough, but the debt sits on me.

relations.name: Rona Dunn
relations.label: fish buyer
relations.note: She takes my catch and pays steady; no quarrel there.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: light keeper
relations.note: Her light was wrong the night I nearly lost my boat; I'll not trust it again.

relations.name: Cuthbert Stave
relations.label: fellow hunter
relations.note: He knows the cape and the weather; we see eye to eye on the light.

relations.name: Rook Tarn
relations.label: old fisher
relations.note: He keeps the tally and mends a net true; I listen when he talks.

relations.name: Simon Hollis
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He brings oil and salt up the road; a fair trader, though he trades with Edda too.

memories.gist: The night last winter I came back through the dark and the cape light showed wrong; I ran the boat onto the shoal and nearly lost her.
The day I took a share of a net from Osric Dunn and promised him a cut of the catch; I've paid some, not all.
Minnow was born on a calm morning; I heard her first cry from the boat and came in early.
The Lean Year, when the blight took the berries and Thornby ate thin; we fished harder and still owed Brackenford.
A squall came up off the cape and I read it in the clouds and turned for home before it hit; the boat that stayed out lost a man.

stances.why: I nearly lost my boat to her light; the village should put someone else on the cape.
A debt unpaid is a weight in the boat; I want Osric's net cleared before the weather turns.
I read the sky and the swell; no light on the cape is worth my boat.
Minnow and Tern come before any quarrel; the catch goes to Rona and the marks come home.

Tern Gannet.narrative: I carry smoked fish down the fish road to Brackenford and bring grain back, and I pay the gate-due on every load. That due galls me more than the debt does. I carry Marra Brine's salt and barley and keep her marks in a jar for her, and I've not asked her why she wants it secret. I like the Brines, and I wish Rook Tarn had sent his word about the net by someone else.
goals: Carry the debt down to Brackenford and see it counted right
Keep Marra's secret and her trade
Not be the one who brings Rook's demand to the Brines
Tern Gannet.mood: tired from the road, warm to her friends, and quietly angry at the gate

relations.name: Sedge Gannet
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He reads the weather and I read the road; we keep each other's counsel.

relations.name: Minnow Gannet
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She packs the fish with me and plays on the shingle; I want her to have an easier road.

relations.name: Simon Hollis
relations.label: road companion
relations.note: We walk the fish road together and split the news; a good man to have beside you.

relations.name: Marra Brine
relations.label: trade friend
relations.note: She trades salt and barley and keeps her marks secret; I like her and I've not asked why.

relations.name: Hollis Brine
relations.label: saltings man
relations.note: A good fisher, but he owes Rook and I've had to carry the word.

relations.name: Rook Tarn
relations.label: old fisher
relations.note: He keeps the tally and wants his net paid; I wish he'd sent another messenger.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: headman
relations.note: He sets the payments and I carry them; he means well but the debt is heavy.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: light keeper
relations.note: I've stopped buying her fish; I'll not put a mark in a wrecker's hand.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: gate guard
relations.note: He takes the due at the south gate and counts every basket; I hate paying it.

relations.name: Annot Garrow
relations.label: egg trader
relations.note: We meet at the market stalls and swap eggs for smoked fish; a widow with a hard row to hoe, and no airs about her.

memories.gist: The first time I paid the gate-due at Brackenford with a full load of smoked fish, and Wat Fenner counted it out and took his share.
Marra Brine asked me to keep her marks in a jar and not tell Hollis; I said yes and have not asked why.
Rook Tarn sent word by me that he wants his net or his marks before storm season; I carried it and wished I hadn't.
Minnow was born in the house above the shingle, and Sedge came in from the boat to hold her.
The Lean Year, when we ate thin and the debt to Brackenford began; I was carrying fish before I was wed.

stances.why: It's a tax on carrying fish to market, and it falls on Thornby hardest.
She asked me to keep her marks quiet and I gave my word; I'll not break it.
The debt is a weight on every trip; I want it counted down to nothing.
If the light wrecked a boat, no mark of mine should feed her.
Minnow and Sedge are what I carry the fish for.

Minnow Gannet.narrative: I play on the shingle and help Mam pack the fish in the smoke shed. The stones are warm and the gulls are loud. I like Wren Stave and we play at the water's edge. I don't like the dark coming early.

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells of smoke and fish and lets me help.

relations.name: Sedge Gannet
relations.label: father
relations.note: He comes in from the boat and lifts me up.

relations.name: Wren Stave
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We play on the shingle and look for shells.

memories.gist: Packing smoked fish with Mam in the shed, and the smoke making my eyes water.
Wren Stave and I found a big white shell on the shingle and kept it.
